subject: Request: temporary rate lift & 72h traffic forecast for Velotech launch
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Kumar <aisha.kumar@velotech.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 28 Sep 2025 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary rate lift & 72h traffic forecast for Velotech launch

Hi Aisha / Velotech launch team —

Congrats on the scheduled push to prod. Per our onboarding checklist, Velotech is requesting a short-term increase to their per-tenant token and concurrency limits for the first 72 hours of launch. I need to coordinate the internal ops/product asks so we can approve a temporary rate lift and set routing/guardrails.

Quick context: Velotech expects a burst of background inference plus interactive sessions that could double their current peak qps for the first day and remain ~1.3x for the next 48h. They provided a raw traffic outline (attached).

Asks:
- Internal: can Product confirm which model variants we should allow for automatic fallback (gpt-like-3-quant vs gpt-like-3-full)?
- Internal: SRE/Quota: what exact per-tenant TPS/concurrency ceilings we can safely grant for 72h without impacting other tenants?
- Internal/Sales: pricing impact / temporary overage treatment (billing or credit?)
- External: Aisha, can you confirm expected peak qps and any known cron/batch jobs that will hit us during the 72h window? If you can provide a tighter 6h-by-6h projection that'd help.

Attachments: [Attachment: velotech_72h_forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet, 84KB)]

Proposed next steps: we aim to lock numbers within 12 hours and schedule a 30-min ops call tomorrow. Please flag if any compliance or region constraints we should know about.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Account Lead, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Aisha Kumar <aisha.kumar@velotech.io>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Sep 2025 18:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary rate lift & 72h traffic forecast for Velotech launch

Thanks Naomi — quick answers below.

Peak: we anticipate ~1,600 qps total at peak minute 1 (mostly background + interactive), baseline is ~800 qps today.
Known batch jobs: yes — two nightly ingestion jobs at 02:00 and 03:30 PT that hit batching endpoints for embeddings (~200 concurrent calls, bursty for ~15 minutes each).
Fallback model: we prefer to allow the quantized variant as a fallback for throughput reasons; however high-quality generation should use full variant for interactive flows.

I can produce a 6h-by-6h breakdown by morning. We also included a short runbook with the forecast (see attached).

Aisha
Head of Platform, Velotech
[Velotech Launch Team]
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, Aisha Kumar <aisha.kumar@velotech.io>
Date: Mon, 29 Sep 2025 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary rate lift & 72h traffic forecast for Velotech launch

Thanks — a few product/ops clarifications from my side:

- Quota mechanics: our temporary rate lift options are per-tenant TPS + token-rate cap. We can also set a hard concurrency cap on streaming sessions.
- Safe headroom for 72h (without cluster resize): +1.5x on TPS for tenants in the us-west cluster if we limit fallback to quantized variants and enable KV cache for repeated prefixes.
- If Velotech requires full model fallback for interactive sessions, we should cap simultaneous interactive sessions to 150 to protect tail latency.

Action: I will draft two numeric proposals (conservative / aggressive) and attach recommended guardrail settings.

-Ben
Product Ops Engineer

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, ben_carter@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: Aisha Kumar <aisha.kumar@velotech.io>
Date: Mon, 29 Sep 2025 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary rate lift & 72h traffic forecast for Velotech launch

Uploading the consolidated forecast & playbook (attached). Highlights:
- 72h requested window: 2025-10-02 00:00 PT -> 2025-10-05 00:00 PT (Velotech asked for 72h from their launch kickoff)
- Conservative proposal: TPS cap = 1,200; concurrency = 120; token-rate = 2,000 tokens/sec
- Aggressive proposal: TPS cap = 1,800; concurrency = 240; token-rate = 3,500 tokens/sec (requires fast-fallback quantized only)
- Recommended routing: route 70% of background traffic to dedicated burst pool (if available), 30% to hosted with KV caching enabled.

Attachments: [Attachment: velotech_72h_forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet, 92KB)] [Attachment: rate-exception-form.pdf (pdf, 28KB)]

Please note: aggressive numbers will require approval from capacity on-call and an SLA exception for latency SLOs. Jordan — can you advise on billing treatment for the temporary lift?

-Marissa
Senior Partner Solutions

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Aisha Kumar <aisha.kumar@velotech.io>
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 08:29:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary rate lift & 72h traffic forecast for Velotech launch

Billing/finance here — options for temporary treatment:
- Option A (preferred for pilot): waive overage for first 72h and convert excess into a one-time usage credit applied on next invoice.
- Option B: bill at regular overage rate but apply a discretionary credit if SLA/uptime targets are met.

We can approve Option A for strategic pilot accounts (VEL-1234) if Sales confirms this is required to remove friction. Need confirmation by 18:00 PT today so we can process the credit paperwork. Also: we need the signed rate-exception-form (attached) before we enable changes.

-Jordan
Revenue Operations Manager

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Kumar <aisha.kumar@velotech.io>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 01 Oct 2025 11:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary rate lift & 72h traffic forecast for Velotech launch

Thanks all — quick summary and action items:

- Product (Ben): finalize the conservative/aggressive numeric configs by 14:00 PT today.
- Marissa: make the routing playbook ready and add guardrail toggles for KV caching + quantized fallback.
- Jordan: Option A (usage credit) approved for VEL-1234 pending signed rate-exception-form; I'll secure the signature from Velotech.
- Aisha (Velotech): please send the 6h-by-6h breakdown and sign the attached PDF. Once we have the form, ops will enable the temporary lift 1 hour before your kickoff and schedule a 15-min on-call window to monitor.

Aisha — cc'd here is the Doc for signatures. If you prefer, I can route the PDF via DocuSign.

Naomi
Account Lead, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
